correctness.rationale: Proof reconstructed: an edge state zero or two determines both endpoint bits, and a state one propagates the complementary bit. A realized connected observation therefore has one representative unless all edges have state one; the latter has precisely two representatives exactly for bipartite connected components. Independence across components yields factor z per isolate, 2^v per nonbipartite component, and (2^v-2+z) per nontrivial bipartite component. Every multiplicity is a power of two; root factorization retrieves the component-order multiset and coefficients retrieve isolated/nonbipartite counts. Exact enumerations of all 33867 graphs with at most six vertices and 750 sampled larger graphs corroborated every formula. Finite tests are not used as proof of all-graph quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The source-visible novel assertion is the complete factorized unlabeled inverse-fiber polynomial of the vertex-to-edge three-state observation for every finite simple graph, together with a precise recovery/equivalence classification of component-order data. Classical connectivity, bipartite two-coloring, and basic rough-approximation definitions are explicitly acknowledged. Full-text limitations and alternative terminology are documented and prevent a claim of certified global publication priority.

value.rationale: A natural two-sided rough incidence observation on graph edges admits a complete and exact information-loss classification across all finite simple graphs. The unlabelled fiber-size multiset exactly distinguishes which component-order information survives while proving that finer topology is necessarily lost; it also yields exact image size, worst-case ambiguity, and output min-entropy. This is not a parameter swap or a one-off tiny computation. Its structural rank-two feature fails for a single rank-three hyperedge (fiber six), giving a sharp boundary and motivating further study of hypergraph granulations.
